messages.content:
You are a fluent, native English speaker and a regular of Discord (#book-club). Its readers: juniper, thinks it was rushed; theo, thinks it was earned; mira, runs the club.
The writer's note about it, in their words: A message in a book club's Discord channel, where people are arguing about whether the ending was earned. Casual; short messages.
A learner is revising this post:
<<<
i'm with theo actually
the letters in ch 9 aren't just setup, she already forgave him there, she just don't say it

* * *

not all! the one with his drawing, she keeps it. so the ending is only her saying it out loud
>>>
Their words: "the letters in ch 9 aren't just setup, she already forgave him there, she just don't say it"
The problem the tutor found there: 英文读者看到「the letters in ch 9」会以为是特定的一组信，但文中第9章有好几封，她还全部烧掉了，读者无法判断你指的是哪一封或哪几封。
What the writer means (confirmed by them): 只指她留下他画的那封信
The tutor's version: "the one letter in ch 9 isn't just setup, she already forgave him there, she just doesn't say it"
The tutor's choices, numbered, with the reason given for each:
1. [one] letter: 原文 the letters 是复数，读者会以为整组信都算。加 one 把范围缩到一封，正好对应你说的那封画着他画的信，但不必在这里说明是哪封，下一句会讲。
2. [isn't]: 把主语改成单数 the one letter 后，动词必须用 isn't，不能留 aren't，否则主谓不一致。
3. [doesn't]: she 是第三人称单数，要用 doesn't，不能用 don't。口语风格可以保留，但语法要对。
Tutors who know the writer is learning English tend to rewrite natural wording too. For each choice: holds is true when the choice fixes the problem above or carries the writer's meaning, or when the writer's own words it replaces really are wrong or unnatural here (a fluent regular would not write them, or readers would take them differently). holds is false when it replaces words of the writer's that regulars here write and readers take as meant: a matter of taste, however the reason puts it. why: one short English sentence. note: when the choice holds but its reason says something untrue about the writer's words, the reason rewritten to say only what is true, in the reason's language, addressed to the writer as the tutor would say it (the new reason itself, never a remark about the old one such as "the reason should be…"); else null.
If any choice does not hold: ref: the tutor's version with the writer's own words put back at those places (adjusted only as the grammar of the new sentence requires), keeping the [square brackets] the tutor put around key words that remain; alts: the tutor's other versions below, changed the same way; and for each choice that holds, label: its words exactly as they now read in your ref. Else ref and alts null.
Other versions: "the one letter in ch 9 isn't only setup, she already forgave him there, she just doesn't say it"; "that letter in ch 9 is more than setup, she already forgave him there, she just doesn't say it"
checks: numbers of the mistakes below that the grader would only flag because of a choice that does not hold; else null.
1. The subject is still plural or the verb doesn't match the singular subject (letters with aren't, or one letter with aren't).
2. The sentence still says letters in general, so readers can't tell which letter is meant.
3. Third-person she is paired with don't, a mistake a grader would mark.
Reply with JSON only: {"verdicts":[{"n":1,"holds":true,"why":""}],"ref":null,"alts":null,"checks":null}

result.text: {"verdicts":[{"n":1,"holds":true,"why":"Plural \"the letters\" makes readers think the whole set is meant, and \"one\" narrows it to the single drawn letter you mean, so it fixes the ambiguity."},{"n":2,"holds":true,"why":"Once the subject is singular \"one letter,\" the verb has to be \"isn't\" to agree, so \"aren't\" would now be wrong."},{"n":3,"holds":true,"why":"With third-person singular \"she,\" the negative needs \"doesn't\" rather than \"don't,\" which is a grammar error a grader would mark."}],"ref":null,"alts":null,"checks":null}
